==English==

===Etymology===
From {{inh|en|enm|representative}}, from {{der|en|frm|representatif}} and its etymon {{der|en|la-med|repraesentātīvus}}.<ref>{{R:OED Online|pos=''adj.'' and ''n.''|noformat=1|id=6753272964}}</ref> {{surf|en|represent|-ative}}; See [[representation]]. Displaced native {{noncog|ang|spala||a representative}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˌɹɛpɹɪˈzɛnt(ət)ɪv/}}
** {{audio|en|en-us-representative.ogg|a=US}}
* {{hyph|en|rep|re|sen|ta|tive}}

===Adjective===
{{en-adj}}

# Typical; having the same properties or interest as a larger group.
#* '''c. 1977''', {{w|Carl Parker (politician)|Carl Parker}} (attributed quote)
# Representing, showing a [[likeness]].
#: {{ux|en|Are you sure this paper is '''representative''' of your child's writing?}}
#: {{ux|en|the '''representative''' faculty of the human imagination}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# ''A delegate.''
## Someone who [[represent]]s others as a [[member]] of a [[legislative]] or [[govern]]ing [[body]]. {{defdate|from 17th c.}}
##: {{ux|en|She served four terms as '''representative''' of her local at the national union convention.}}
##* {{quote-video game|en|developer=w:BioWare|title={{w|Mass Effect (video game)|Mass Effect}}|location=Redwood City|publisher=Electronic Arts|year=2008|system=PC|scene=Quarians: Government Codex entry|isbn=9780784546642|oclc=246633669|text=Each vessel in the Fleet has the right to send '''representatives''' to the Conclave aboard the flagship. The number of '''representatives''' is based on crew size. Larger clans, with bigger ships and more votes, form the cores of political blocs. Opposition comes from the Outriders' Coalition, with delegates from thousands of smaller ships.}}
## One who [[speak for|speaks for]] or acts [[on behalf of]] another in a particular (especially official) capacity. {{defdate|from 17th c.}}
##: {{ux|en|I will send a '''representative''' to work out the details of the contract.}}
## {{lb|en|legal}} An [[heir]]. {{defdate|from 17th c.}}
##* {{RQ:Smollett Peregrine Pickle|volume=I|1|text=This pathetic remonstrance had the desired effect upon his '''representative''', who spared no pains to fulfill the request of the deceased {{...}}.}}
## {{lb|en|US|politics}} Specifically, a member of the {{w|United States House of Representatives}}. {{defdate|from 18th c.}}
##: {{ux|en|All '''representatives''' face re-election every two years.}}
## A [[company]] [[agent]] who visits potential purchasers; a [[salesman]]. {{defdate|from 20th c.}}
##: {{syn|en|minister|q1=formal or literary}}
## {{lb|en|UK|tourism}} A worker at a [[holiday]] [[resort]] who escorts [[guest]]s and leads activities.
# ''Something standing for something else.''
## Something [[representing]] or standing for another; a [[symbol]], an [[embodiment]]. {{defdate|from 17th c.}}
##* {{RQ:Landon Lady Anne Granard|pages=131–133|volume=I|passage=The furniture was the same when she married..[ ]..The only '''representatives''' of to-day, were two large and comfortable arm-chairs, and a few elegant-looking trifles, the work of the Misses Granard.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=1978|last=Kołakowski|first=Leszek|authorlink=Leszek Kołakowski|title=w:Main Currents of Marxism|volume=II: The Golden Age|origlang=pl|original=Główne nurty marksizmu: rozwój|translator=P[aul] S[teven] Falla|origyear=1976|publisher=w:Clarendon Press|location=w:Oxford|isbn=9780198245698|oclc=961252281|page=390|pageurl=https://archive.org/details/maincurrentsofma00lesz/page/390|passage={{...}} whereas a tiny group with no roots in the working class was entitled, so long as it professed the Marxist ideology, to declare itself the sole '''representative''' of the proletariat and the sole embodiment of proletarian consciousness.}}
## A [[member]] of a particular [[class]].
### Something (especially a [[living]] [[organism]]) [[regard]]ed as [[typical]] of its [[class]]; a [[type]]. {{defdate|from 17th c.}}
### {{lb|en|mathematics}} A consistent choice of element from an equivalence class, used to identify it.
## A [[substitute]] or [[analogue]]. {{defdate|from 17th c.}}
